sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: This species is close to I. phallicaecalis; like the latter, its soldier and worker are characterised by a phallus-shaped caecum, the caecum sending forward a finger-like projection whose distal end may be inflated or cap-like, coronate. The alate caecum, although not phallus-shaped, is also better developed than in the alates of other species, forming a forward-directed comma shape. The soldiers of the two are similar in morphology, differing only slightly in mandibular curvature, but their ecology differs: this species occurs in forest galleries, I. phallicaecalis in mainland evergreen forest. The worker enteric valve architecture (EVA) is of the finitimus type, the workers among the smallest in the genus, the head capsule averaging narrower than in I. phallicaecalis. The soldier can be separated from I. phallicaecalis by its shorter left mandible: left mandible ventral length SMlL = 1.99–2.36 mm (2.17–2.53 mm in I. phallicaecalis); its EVA is generally recognisable as the finitimus type. The alate averages, together with I. fungifaber, among the smallest in the genus: head width including compound eyes IHdW = 1.38–1.54 mm. All specimens come from gallery forest in the south-east of the Congo forest.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Description based on 14 alates from 9 colonies (5 female alates, 6 male alates, 2 queens, 1 male), the wings on 9 individuals only. Head capsule well sclerotized, very dark (C6–C8), paler in long-preserved specimens; frontal gland pore concolorous with the head capsule or slightly paler; postclypeus C5–C7, usually one shade paler than the head capsule; antennae C4–C6. Pronotum C5–C7, concolorous with the postclypeus, usually one shade paler than the head capsule; meso- and metanotum C5–C7; legs C4–C5, the tibiae concolorous with the femora or one shade darker; wings transparent with a brown to grey tinge (Cf2–Cf4), the costa darker; abdominal tergites C5–C6; sternites distinctly paler in the middle (C3–C4), darker at the sides (C4–C5), the posterior sternites (C4–C5) darker than the anterior ones. Head capsule with conspicuous setae scattered among the dense felt of short fine hairs; labrum and postclypeus with conspicuous setae mixed with short hairs; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, most segments with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at the tip, especially distally (visible above 50×). Pronotum setae mainly on the margins, shorter in the middle; meso- and metanotum with fine pale hairs arranged along the median band (generally visible at 40× or 80×), the metanotal posterior lobe often with several larger setae. Legs hairy, the fore coxa with 8–10 stronger setae, the trochanter with 5–6; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, the tibiae with 20–30 spines. Abdominal tergites with setae of mixed sizes; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward, together with many long and small setae directed posteriorly. Compound eyes nearly circular; ocelli short-oval to oval, separated from the compound eye by about 0.9–1.5 times the small ocellar diameter; frontal gland pore generally a small circular or elongate mark. Antennae 16-segmented in alates, the queen and male with 3–4 fewer segments through breakage. Labrum domed. Left mandible apical tooth on average shorter than in most species of the genus, but always more prominent than the first marginal tooth; 3 marginal teeth, the second expressed only as an undulation of the tooth margin between the first and third; only the apical tooth sharp in unworn specimens; the proximal premolar hidden or partly hidden by the molar prominence in dorsal view; the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process. Right mandible apical tooth always more prominent than the first marginal tooth; 2 marginal teeth, the first sharp-tipped when fresh, the second smaller and blunt even when fresh; the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum distinctly wider than long, narrower than the head width (including compound eyes), flat to very weakly saddle-shaped, the anterior lobe short and very slightly raised; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a ridge. Wings: R1 completely fused with the margin and sclerotized; Rs single and sclerotized; M and Cu unsclerotized or weakly sclerotized, with 2–4 and 9–12 branches respectively. Measurements: compound eye major diameter 0.34–0.41 mm, head width including compound eyes 1.38–1.54 mm, distance from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth 0.17–0.21 mm, ocellus major diameter 0.12–0.17 mm, postclypeus width 0.65–0.77 mm, pronotum width 1.18–1.39 mm, fore wing length to the suture 12.4–13.9 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text: Head capsule on the pale side (Cf4–Cf5), darker in long-preserved specimens (e.g. Cf5–Cf6); always grading from a darker frons to a paler posterior, often rather abruptly, so that the head capsule may look bicoloured; antennae and labrum 1–2 shades paler than the frons; mandibles dark (C7–C8), the base generally abruptly two shades paler and generally paler than the frons; thorax and legs generally concolorous with the head capsule (C3–C5) or slightly paler; abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents, the tergites sometimes with a pale yellow tinge. Head capsule with a few scattered setae; a dense tuft of hairs surrounds and covers the frontal gland pore; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, the apical segment with a tuft of very fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); the labrum always with 4–5 large setae on each lateral lobe; pronotum and mesonotum with few setae, mainly on the margins. Fore coxa with 4–7 spines on the ridge and none ventrally; trochanter generally with 1–4 spines and rows of setae; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, each tibia with a row of 8–12 spines. Abdominal tergites with the large setae mainly on the posterior margin; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward and often pigmented, together with smaller setae directed posteriorly. Soldier medium-sized within the genus. Head capsule distinctly sclerotized, distinctly longer than wide; in dorsal view the sides usually nearly parallel, narrowing in the posterior quarter (sometimes markedly), converging from the antennal sockets towards the mandible bases, the posterior margin regularly rounded, sometimes with 3 short straight or even concave sections; the upper margin concave; the angle between the projecting mandibles and the frons always slightly obtuse; frons generally without an anterior swelling. Gulamentum narrowing in the posterior half in ventral view, the anterior half widening at sharp angles or ear-like at the sides. Antennae 15-segmented, rarely 14. Labrum always deeply forked, wider than long, the sides generally harp-shaped; the lobes angular, their tips fine, white or semitransparent; the anterior margin concave. Mandibles sabre-like, of medium curvature within the genus; the inner margin generally smooth, each mandible with 1 distinct but very small marginal tooth near the molar area; mandibles distinctly shorter than the head; the surface of both smooth and shining; the right mandible generally more curved than the left. Pronotum saddle-shaped, 57%–63% of the head width, the anterior and posterior margins generally entire; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Enteric valve inserted on the left side, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen. Caecum always fairly well developed (as in the worker), best seen in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, a typical finger-like projection extending forward, sometimes inflated or cap-like distally. Primary cushions (PC) arranged with trigonal symmetry, the odd cushion about 20% longer than the even ones, the crest being the place where the setae abruptly become very dense (compare the worker EVA). Measurements: head dorsal concavity sagitta 0.00–0.07 mm, head length 2.42–3.21 mm, head width 1.74–2.15 mm, left mandible ventral length 1.99–2.36 mm, left mandible minor curvature 0.19–0.33 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale (C1–C3), turning grey in long-preserved specimens; proximal antennal segments pale (C2–C3), the apical segment always 1–2 shades darker (C4–C5); thorax, tergites and legs pale (C1–C3); abdomen grey to red-brown from the gut contents. Head capsule and postclypeus with a few scattered erect setae; labrum with a few scattered stout setae; antennae with conspicuous setae and more numerous small hairs, the apical segment with a tuft of fine curved hairs at its tip (visible above 50×); thoracic tergites with scattered setae. Fore coxa always ridged, with 1 fine seta, 3–6 spines on the ridge and 0–3 ventrally; fore trochanter with 5–7 spines; fore, mid and hind tibiae with 3, 2 and 2 apical spurs and 0, 2 and 0 subapical spurs respectively, and with a row of 8–15 spines. Abdominal tergites with scattered setae; sternites with long setae erect or slightly inclined forward and often pigmented, together with smaller setae directed posteriorly. Workers small within the genus. Head capsule weakly sclerotized (except the mandibles). Antennae 14–14.5 segmented. Labrum domed. Left mandible with a well-developed apical tooth, sharp-tipped when fresh; 3 marginal teeth, the first well developed but blunt even when fresh, the second weak (expressed only as an undulating tooth margin, lost with wear), the third with a blunt tip; the proximal premolar partly hidden by the molar prominence; the dorsal surface of the molar with a rounded prominence ending posteriorly in a small sharp process. Right mandible with a well-developed apical tooth, sharp when fresh; 2 marginal teeth, the first well developed and sharp when fresh, the second smaller and blunt even when fresh; the molar with a rounded labial process ventrally and heel-shaped posteriorly. Pronotum saddle-shaped, 66%–73% of the head width; the fore coxa with a lip-like projection ventrally forming a sharp ridge. Enteric valve inserted on the left, best seen in ventral view, in the posterior half of the abdomen. Primary cushions arranged in the finitimus type with trigonal symmetry: the downstream part of the odd cushion is broad, its bulbous inflation bearing denser shorter setae; supporting setae numerous, 19–32 on each side of the odd cushion; secondary cushions broad upstream, distinctly narrowing downstream, the spines evenly distributed. Caecum always fairly well developed, best seen in ventral view, near the middle of the abdomen, a typical finger-like projection extending forward, sometimes inflated or cap-like distally. Measurements: maximum head width 1.06–1.27 mm, distance from the apical tooth to the first marginal tooth 0.15–0.19 mm, left mandible functional length 0.49–0.58 mm, mean length of primary cushions 1–6 0.46–0.62 mm, mean width 0.06–0.09 mm, mean length of secondary cushions 0.36–0.48 mm, mean width 0.17–0.28 mm, odd primary cushion elongation index WVPOdd-Elg = 5.90–10.1.

note: Adapted from the genus revision in Josens et al. (2025), original in English; measurements from Table 11 and the text of the original; distribution, hosts, DNA and figure numbers are not translated.
